summary: All 16 claimed orbits are genuine collisionless periodic orbits with the claimed minimal period and words; they form 9 new words, (Ba)^n(bA)^n for n = 4..12 (rungs k = 3..11). Novelty was checked against the Li-Liao corpus and the Suvakov-Dmitrasinovic orbits; the Sofia group's equal-mass databases could not be opened.

cards.title: Periodic
cards.text: An independent code (DOP853 at 10⁻¹³, and implicit Radau IIA for the first 16) closes every orbit to between 10⁻¹¹ and 8×10⁻⁹, and the residual shrinks as the tolerance tightens. Newton moves our values by at most 10⁻¹² in velocity. Each stated period is the shortest one, and no orbit comes closer than 0.025 to a collision.

cards.title: Named correctly
cards.text: For the first 16 orbits, a second topology code, written from scratch with two different ways of reading the crossings, reproduces every word exactly, under both labelling conventions that match the published words of known orbits. Every crossing of the equator is clean, far from the collision points. The 7 rungs added later carry the same words, computed by our own code.

cards.title: Not in the catalogues
cards.text: None of the rung words for k = 3 to 11 matches any of the 2,360 words in the Li & Liao catalogues under any physical symmetry (rotation, time reversal, mirror image, swapping the equal stars). At m₃ = 0.5 and 0.75 no catalogued orbit has the same word or a period within 1%, although these rungs lie inside the window the 2018 survey searched.

cards.title: Anchored to known orbits
cards.text: Following rung 1 from m₃ = 0.25 upward lands on Li, Jing & Liao's I.A i.c. 2 at m₃ = 0.75 and on Li & Liao's equal-mass I.A i.c. 3, both to every published digit. This is an end-to-end check of the search, the continuation and the slice conventions.

cards.title: Not yet checked
cards.text: We could not open the Sofia group's equal-mass databases (Hristov, Hristova and coauthors, 2022–2025). Their 2022 high-precision set contains the rung-2 word at equal masses. If the higher rungs also reach m₃ = 1, some of these words could already be in their 2024 database of 6,333 equal-mass orbits.

cards.title: Not new
cards.text: Periods that grow in step with word length are the topological dependence of Kepler's third law (Dmitrašinović & Šuvakov 2015). Ladders of words are known too, for example (BA)ⁿ(ba)ⁿ. What is new here is these rungs and orbits, not the pattern.
